items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Happy Caldwell) is narrating a conversation with Benny Morton, who mentions earning more with Fletcher Henderson. Happy Caldwell himself does not claim a personal relationship with Fletcher Henderson, only that he knows of the financial arrangement Benny Morton described.

ctx.x: Well, the only thing -- a few years ago, four or five years ago George Weill had got some college gigs he got some colleagues' tapes in New Jersey, and he wanted -- I think there was four or five things or something, you know. They were like concerts. And he wanted many more Benny Morton. And he said, do you know where Benny Morton (unintelligible) is? And I said yes, and I called Benny, and I said, do you (unintelligible) want this thing. And it was $300.00.

So Benny said, well, I wouldn't mind. I wouldn't mind it. This was, you know, a few years ago, four years ago, five maybe. But he said, no, I used to earn more than that with Fletcher Henderson. And I said, well -- he said, no, he said, I think I ought to -- I ought not to sort of sell myself that cheap. Well, I've heard that before (unintelligible), Fletcher made an awful lot of money (unintelligible).
